trickyParts: pgx runs a batch's callbacks in order in results.Close() and returns the first error. The issue row is queued first, so a missing key still answers its pgx.ErrNoRows (404). A statement's own failure reaches its callback through rows.Err(), so the scans check rows.Err() first and wrap it as the sequential path wraps its Query error.

Each batch's results are closed before anything else uses the pool. store.Pool.SendBatch does not mark the context as holding a connection, and pool.go is left alone because sjawhar/legion#2402 rewrites it. Whichever merges second keeps both.

The forward merge of main (de546ed2) met main's #2458, which moved inlineWithEscapes, readBackReaders, readsBackUnder and holdsTilde from render_inline.go to run_spellings.go. The merge takes main's render_inline.go and applies cleanups 2 and 4 to run_spellings.go.
Parse gives block ids at random, so the render corpus comparison masks uuids by order of appearance within each document.

findings: 1 queueApprovals (reviews.go) is the one approval queue-and-apply: queueArtifactDetails queues versions then calls it (apply: versions first); attachApprovals sends it as a batch of its own (one round trip per attachApproval in requestArtifactApproval's transaction); loadArtifactRow calls loadArtifactDetails for its one artifact. roundFour.roundTrips: Measured with the traced pool (count_artifact_reads_test.go, throwaway, in the round 4 evidence): GET /api/v1/artifacts/{id} and GET /api/v1/issues/{key}/artifacts/{slug} of a document take 4 round trips at cd2e246d and 2 at 1b91d67f (the row, then one batch of versions, latest review, open approval request); of a file, 2 at both.
roundFour.transactionalBatch: requestArtifactApproval (POST /api/v1/artifacts/{id}/approval-requests) now sends two batches on its pgx.Tx, the second after it opened or renewed the ask. Every read before each batch has run to its end (loadArtifact, requireOpenOwner, settledVersionNumber, OpenApprovalAsk return values, not cursors), so no open cursor meets either batch. TestApprovalRequestsReadTheirApprovalInTheirTransactionInSequenceAndAtOnce drives it in sequence, on seven documents at once and sixteen times at once on one document, with a 90 s bound, and checks each document awaiting and the pool empty afterwards; it passes three times under -race and fails (first request 500) when attachApprovals leaves its batch unclosed.
